verdict.reasoning: Patient reports 'a sore, and a red skin... really itchy... super annoying' and that it has been 'a few days' and later both agree it started 'four days ago'; he asks for 'something quick to solve it.'

Patient states rash is on 'my chest, my, my hands, my arms' and clarifies 'just the chest, hands and like, like inside the elbows'; when asked about face: 'On my face? No.' Antecubital fossae correspond to 'inside the elbows.'

Patient says 'I can't even sleep at night' and at work 'I can't focus... I'm always like, uh, disturbed by this disease'; also 'I like, for instance hiking... I can't really do it anymore, because it's like very... super painful.'
Patient: 'my skin is a bit cracked in some parts, like kind of cracked' and denies 'any other pus or blood, coming out of your skin' with 'No.'

To systemic review questions: 'any temperature or fevers?' – 'No. just very itchy.'; 'Your bowels are working OK?' – implied yes with no concerns; 'Your chest is OK? No cough, no breathing difficulties?' – Patient: 'No.'; 'You're passing urine OK.' – Patient: 'I I think so.'
Patient: 'I was like prescribed for my eczema'; later: 'apart from the eczema, do you have any other medical problems?' Patient: 'no. I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore.'

Doctor: 'do you take any regular medications at the moment?' Patient: 'Uh no.' Patient also says 'I bought a, a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night... it didn't help' and later 'I have tried uh antihistamines, but uh but it didn't really help.'
Doctor: 'do you have any allergies at all?' Patient: 'Ohh, allergies. Uh, no.' This supports no known drug allergies.
Patient: 'I live with a few flatmates... I'm thirty one... I'm living with a few people to save money' and 'I work uh at a pharmaceutical company... I'm a, like a kind of project manager.'
Doctor: 'do you smoke at all?' Patient: 'No.' Regarding alcohol: 'once in a while... a few, a few beers per week... Nothing, nothing crazy.'

Doctor: 'I do wonder whether this is a flare-up of your eczema' based on 'quite itchy' rash 'mainly your chest' and later summary 'chest, hands and... inside the elbows'; earlier ROS shows 'No... temperature or fevers?' and 'No cough, no breathing difficulties,' indicating no systemic symptoms.
Patient directly links itch to sleep: 'it's itching a lot, like all the time. And I can't even sleep at night,' indicating sleep disturbance secondary to pruritus.
Doctor: 'You mentioned using steroid creams, yesterday... I wonder whether giving you a stronger prescription of a of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today.'

Doctor: 'I'm going to give you something, some emollients, which helps to moisturize the skin... which use in the bath and shower... it's definitely worth um using that for the first seven to ten days before we make the decision on whether it's working or not.'

Doctor: 'It's also worth um using antihistamines... Things like Loratadine or Piriton' and later 'I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Um, something like Fexofenadine, which I can give to you today.'

Doctor: 'it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms, anything you wear or anything you use, in terms of shower gels or soap. Because if that's causing your symptoms, then we need to have a discussion...' This supports a trigger diary to identify and avoid irritants.
Doctor: 'using the steroids and the emollients... over the next week to ten days, should hopefully control your symptoms. But do come back and see me next week, if things don't get better.'
